SYSTEMS PROGRAMMING AND MACHINE ORGANIZATION
Chapter 30 — Cache Behavior
VERBATIM GRADUATE LECTURE TRANSCRIPT
Charles Dorner

SLIDE 1: Chapter 30 — Cache Behavior

LECTURE NARRATION
Cache behavior is a sequence-dependent property. A cache starts in some state, each access either finds a usable resident block or requires additional work, and each insertion or update changes the state seen by later accesses. A hit rate without the access trace and initial conditions can be misleading.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, cache behavior is a sequence-dependent property.

SLIDE 4: 30.1 Cache hit

LECTURE NARRATION
A hit occurs when the requested block is present in a usable cache entry. The model can satisfy the access at that level. A hit does not imply zero cost; lookup, data delivery, dependencies, and other execution constraints remain. For writes in a coherent machine, a resident line may still require permission acquisition or coordination. The simple examples in this chapter use reads so that tag residency is sufficient to classify a hit.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
A cache is like keeping the things you use most often on your desk instead of walking to a storage room every time.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 6: 30.2 Cache miss

LECTURE NARRATION
A miss occurs when the consulted cache cannot satisfy the request from a usable resident entry. The system obtains the block from another source, potentially another cache, another core, or memory, depending on the hierarchy and coherence state. The cost is not necessarily a full trip to DRAM. An L1 miss that hits in L2 differs from a last-level miss. State which cache level is being discussed and whether a miss rate is local to that level or relative to all original accesses.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
A cache is like keeping the things you use most often on your desk instead of walking to a storage room every time.

SLIDE 8: 30.3 Hit rate

LECTURE NARRATION
Hit rate is hits divided by accesses for the stated cache and interval. If 90 of 100 accesses hit, the rate is 90%. A cold-start interval can have a lower rate than steady state even when the repeated workload is unchanged. Aggregate hit rate can conceal expensive phases or uneven requests. A large number of cheap hits does not necessarily compensate for a small number of extremely costly misses on a critical dependency chain.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, hit rate is hits divided by accesses for the stated cache and interval.

SLIDE 10: 30.4 Miss rate

LECTURE NARRATION
Miss rate is misses divided by accesses. In the simple model where each access is exactly one hit or miss, it equals 1 - hit_rate . Multilevel rates require careful denominators: an L2 local miss rate counts misses among requests that reached L2. If L1 misses on 10% of original accesses and L2 misses on 20% of those, then 2% of original accesses miss both levels. Adding 10% and 20% would be the wrong calculation.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, miss rate is misses divided by accesses.

SLIDE 12: 30.5 Compulsory misses

LECTURE NARRATION
A compulsory miss is the first access to a block in a cold-cache reference model. The block has not yet been brought into the cache by a prior access in that model. Larger lines can reduce the number of distinct blocks for a sequential region but can also fetch unused bytes. Prefetching changes when a block is brought in and how demand misses are observed. It does not make data transfer disappear. When classifying misses, state whether the model includes prefetching and what initial cache state is assumed.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, a compulsory miss is the first access to a block in a cold-cache reference model.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 14: 30.6 Capacity misses

LECTURE NARRATION
A capacity miss occurs because the useful working set exceeds the cache’s available storage under the chosen reference model. Even a fully associative cache of the same capacity cannot retain everything needed across the reuse interval. The common three-category classification compares behavior against a fully associative reference cache with a specified replacement policy, often LRU. Classification depends on that reference. It is not a universal label attached permanently to an address.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, a capacity miss occurs because the useful working set exceeds the cache’s available storage under the chosen reference model.

SLIDE 16: 30.7 Conflict misses

LECTURE NARRATION
A conflict miss arises from restricted placement in sets when a fully associative reference cache of the same capacity would have retained the block. Repeated collisions can cause misses even when the total active block count is no greater than cache capacity. The compulsory/capacity/conflict model is useful but incomplete for coherent multiprocessors. Invalidations, sharing, prefetch interactions, and other effects can introduce additional causes. Do not force every hardware event into a three-category model that deliberately excludes those mechanisms.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, a conflict miss arises from restricted placement in sets when a fully associative reference cache of the same capacity would have retained the block.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 18: Worked example — A small executable cache model

LECTURE NARRATION
The following direct-mapped model has four lines of 16 bytes each. The trace accesses byte addresses 0, 16, 0, 64, 0, 16 . Blocks 0 and 4 both map to slot 0, while block 1 maps to slot 1. Companion listing: ch30/cache.py The output is M M H M M H , followed by hits=2 misses=4 . First references to blocks 0, 1, and 4 are compulsory misses. The later miss on block 0 is a conflict miss relative to a four-line fully associative LRU cache, which could retain all three blocks. The overall hit rate is 2/6 , approximately 33.3%. No cycle count follows from that percentage alone. A cost model is needed to translate the event sequence into a time estimate.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
A cache is like keeping the things you use most often on your desk instead of walking to a storage room every time.

SLIDE 20: Worked example — Classifying first and repeated misses

LECTURE NARRATION
The first access to a never-seen cache block is compulsory. If the working set exceeds total cache capacity and a block is evicted because too much distinct data is active, the later miss can be capacity-related. If two blocks collide in the same limited-associativity set despite enough total capacity, the misses are conflicts.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, the first access to a never-seen cache block is compulsory.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 22: Worked example — Computing hit rate

LECTURE NARRATION
If 9,600 of 10,000 accesses hit, the hit rate is 9600/10000 = 96% and miss rate is 4%. This aggregate alone does not explain performance: where misses go, whether they overlap, and whether they are instruction or data misses also matter.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, if 9,600 of 10,000 accesses hit, the hit rate is 9600/10000 = 96% and miss rate is 4%.

SLIDE 24: Guided lab and review

LECTURE NARRATION
Lab 30. Add a reset method that invalidates every line. Compare the original trace with a second immediate repetition without resetting. Explain why the first event of the repeated trace changes. Review 1. What is the global miss rate when L1’s local miss rate is 5% and L2’s local miss rate is 10%? Review 2. Why is a first-ever access not automatically a demand miss when prefetching is included?

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, lab 30.

SLIDE 26: Chapter Synthesis

LECTURE NARRATION
The chapter's central subject is cache behavior. Correct reasoning requires explicit assumptions, bounds, ownership, and interface contracts. Observed behavior is evidence about a run; it is not automatically a language or system guarantee. Use the worked examples and lab to test whether the model transfers to new cases.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, the chapter's central subject is cache behavior.
